name: ena_update_buf_ring_size
prose: Precondition: adapter is a valid ENA adapter and new_buf_ring_size is the requested TX buf_ring size. It saves the old size, stores the new one in adapter->buf_ring_size, records whether ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP was set, calls ena_down, frees all I/O ring resources and re-initialises the rings with ena_init_io_rings_advanced. In a DEV_NETMAP build it then calls ena_reinit_netmap and returns its code immediately if nonzero (device left down, no reset triggered, no revert). If the device was up it calls ena_up; if that fails it logs, restores the old size, frees and re-initialises the rings again, (in a DEV_NETMAP build calls ena_reinit_netmap again and returns its code if nonzero), sets ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP_BEFORE_RESET and triggers a device reset with ENA_REGS_RESET_OS_TRIGGER; ena_up is not retried. The return value is rc: in a build without DEV_NETMAP it is the ena_up error in the failure case (0 on success); in a DEV_NETMAP build the successful second ena_reinit_netmap call overwrites rc, so after a failed ena_up it returns 0 once the reset has been triggered.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right for DEV_NETMAP builds: rc from ena_up is overwritten by the second ena_reinit_netmap (ena.c:1212-1230 with 1223); without DEV_NETMAP the ena_up error is returned. Original reviewer right that a netmap failure returns early with no revert/reset (1200-1202). Function at 1182-1235 (slice 1021-1276). Read in full.

name: ena_update_queue_size
prose: Precondition: adapter is a valid ENA adapter and new_tx_size and new_rx_size are the requested ring sizes. It stores the old and new requested TX and RX ring sizes, records whether ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP was set, calls ena_down and re-initialises the basic I/O rings (ena_init_io_rings_basic). In a DEV_NETMAP build it calls ena_reinit_netmap and returns its code immediately if nonzero (device left down with the new sizes, nothing reverted, no reset). If the device was up it calls ena_up; if that fails it logs, restores the old requested sizes, re-initialises the basic rings, (with DEV_NETMAP calls ena_reinit_netmap again and returns its code if nonzero), then calls ena_up a second time; if that second call fails it logs, sets ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP_BEFORE_RESET and triggers a device reset with ENA_REGS_RESET_OS_TRIGGER. It returns rc, which at that point is the result of the last ena_up call: 0 if the first ena_up succeeded or the retry with the old sizes succeeded (the first failure is then not reported), nonzero if the retry failed.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong about 'no ena_up retry': a second ena_up call is at ena.c:1279. His other point (rc overwritten) applies to the first ena_up failure, which is overwritten by the retry result (1279) so the prose now says so. Original reviewer right that netmap failure returns early (1256-1258, 1273-1275). Function at 1237-1297 (slice 1021-1276). Read in full.

name: ena_attach
prose: Precondition: pdev is a PCI device whose softc (struct ena_adapter) was allocated by the bus. It initialises defaults in the adapter, allocates a zeroed ena_com_dev (M_WAITOK) and stores it in adapter->ena_dev, and allocates the register BAR. If the register BAR allocation fails it returns ENOMEM after freeing only the ena_com_dev (label err_dev_free; no PCI resources, no ena_bus). It then allocates the separate MSI-X table BAR if its rid differs, returning ENOMEM through err_pci_free (which releases PCI resources and frees ena_dev) on failure. It allocates ena_dev->bus and stores the register tag and handle; if the handle is 0 it returns ENXIO via err_bus_free (frees the bus, releases PCI resources, frees ena_dev). ena_map_llq_mem_bar failure returns its code via err_bus_free; ena_device_init failure returns ENXIO via err_bus_free. After reading features and computing queue sizes, if ena_calc_io_queue_size fails or the maximum IO queue count is not positive it returns EFAULT via err_com_free, which additionally destroys the admin queue, host info and MMIO read request. TX and RX DMA tag setup failures return their codes via err_com_free and err_tx_tag_free (which frees the TX tag first); failure of ena_enable_msix_and_set_admin_interrupts returns its code via err_io_free (frees io ring resources and the RX DMA tag, then continues down through the labels below); failure of ena_com_allocate_customer_metrics_buffer returns its code via err_msix_free (frees stats, resets the device with ENA_REGS_RESET_INIT_ERR, frees the management IRQ and disables MSI-X); failure of ena_sysctl_allocate_customer_metrics_buffer returns its code via err_metrics_buffer_destroy (deletes the metrics buffer, then falls through the remaining labels). Each error path falls through all the later labels, so it performs the cleanup listed for its label and those below it. On success it also allocates stat counters, adds sysctl nodes, sets up the ifnet, creates and starts the reset and metrics taskqueues, with DEV_NETMAP attaches netmap (failure returns its code via err_detach, which detaches the ifnet, removes the media, frees customer_metrics_array and then falls through all the cleanup above), clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE, sets ENA_FLAG_DEVICE_RUNNING, resets the timer and returns 0. On every failure path adapter->ena_dev is left pointing at freed memory once free(ena_dev) has run, and the taskqueues and ifnet created before the netmap step are not torn down except for the ifnet detach on the netmap failure path.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the register BAR failure jumps to err_dev_free (ena.c:3821-3825, 4029-4030) and does not call ena_free_pci_resources. Real function at 3774-4033 (slice 3807-4058 cut the head). Read in full; callees not read, so what ena_free_pci_resources releases is not described.

name: _vnic_dev_cmd2
prose: Precondition: vdev->devcmd2 is an initialised devcmd2 controller (wq_ctrl, cmd_ring, result ring, posted, next_result, color, result_size), cmd is a devcmd word and wait is the number of poll iterations of 100 microseconds each; for write-direction commands the arguments are in vdev->args. It reads the TX fetch index and returns ENODEV if it is 0xFFFFFFFF. It returns EBUSY (after logging that the work queue is full) if advancing the posted index would equal the fetch index. Otherwise it fills the command ring slot at the posted index (cmd, flags, with DEVCMD2_FNORESULT set for _CMD_FLAGS_NOWAIT commands, and for _CMD_DIR_WRITE commands copies VNIC_DEVCMD_NARGS args from vdev->args), writes the new posted index to TX_POSTED_INDEX and stores it in dc2c->posted. If the slot has DEVCMD2_FNORESULT set it returns 0 immediately. Otherwise it takes the result entry at next_result and the current color, advances next_result (wrapping to 0 and flipping color at result_size), and polls up to wait times, 100 us apart, for the result entry's color to match: when it matches and result->error is nonzero it logs it (except for ERR_ECMDUNKNOWN on CMD_CAPABILITY) and returns that error value; when it matches with no error it copies VNIC_DEVCMD2_NARGS result words into vdev->args for _CMD_DIR_READ commands and returns 0. If no match is seen it logs a timeout and returns ETIMEDOUT. The ring slot and result cursor stay advanced in the ETIMEDOUT and error cases. No locks are taken here.
note: Slice started mid-body; the function is _vnic_dev_cmd2 at vnic_dev.c:248-321 (name was unnamed in the packet, read in full). Old prose said the cursor is advanced for no-result commands too; in the code the early return at 284-285 happens before the cursor change at 287-294, so for no-result commands the result cursor is not advanced.

name: evdev_mt_reassign_id
prose: Precondition: evdev and evdev->ev_mt are valid and slot is a valid MT slot index. If id is -1 or the EVDEV_FLAG_MT_KEEPID flag is set, it stores id in mt->tracking_ids[slot] and returns id. Otherwise it reads the slot's current ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID value with evdev_mt_get_value; if that value is not -1 it returns it without changing state (a KASSERT, effective only in kernels with INVARIANTS, requires id to equal mt->tracking_ids[slot] in that case). If the current value is -1 it stores id (not the generated value) in mt->tracking_ids[slot], then repeatedly takes nid = mt->tracking_id++ until no slot in the mt->touches bitmap has an ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID value equal to nid (the loop macro reuses the variable slot as its iterator), and returns that nid. No locks are taken.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the function handles id != -1 with KEEPID clear (evdev_mt.c:549-569), so the old precondition was wrong and is dropped. Round 2 reviewer right about the KASSERT at 556-557; round 1 reviewer right that the input id, not nid, is stored at 561. Function at 543-569 (slice 507-671). Read in full.

name: EXCA_ACCESSOR(slot, SLOT, uint32_t)
prose: Generated function exca_get_slot: a static inline int function taking (device_t dev, uint32_t *t) defined by the EXCA_ACCESSOR(slot, SLOT, uint32_t) invocation, whose body is the single statement return BUS_READ_IVAR(device_get_parent(dev), dev, EXCA_IVAR_SLOT, (uintptr_t *)t). It returns whatever the parent bus's read-ivar method returns for EXCA_IVAR_SLOT (100); on success that method stores the slot value through the cast pointer, which is a uintptr_t pointer aimed at a uint32_t location, so the width written is that of uintptr_t. It performs no checks of its own and takes no locks.
note: Name given as the macro invocation (excavar.h:165) because the function is macro-generated by the definition at 157-163. Old prose said *t is 'left unspecified' on failure; that is not stated in this code since BUS_READ_IVAR's behaviour was not read. Cast of uint32_t* to uintptr_t* at 162 noted as is.

name: pcx_draw
prose: Precondition: adp is a valid video adapter and pcx_info (zlen, zdata, width, height, bpsl, palette) holds a decoded PCX image. Returns 1 immediately if pcx_info.zlen < 1. Otherwise it loads the palette, clears every bank of the framebuffer window by stepping the window origin through the screen (origin < height * bytes-per-scanline) with vidd_set_win_org and bzero, computes the centred position x,y and the window origin and in-window offset pos for it, and then, for each of pcx_info.height scanlines, run-length decodes up to pcx_info.bpsl bytes from zdata into a local line buffer of MAXSCANLINE bytes; it returns 1 if a run header is at the end of the data or a run would exceed pcx_info.bpsl. After decoding a scanline it advances the window by banksize if pos > banksize; then if pos + pcx_info.width exceeds banksize it copies the first banksize - pos bytes, advances origin by banksize, subtracts banksize from pos, repositions the window with vidd_set_win_org and copies the remaining pcx_info.width - j bytes to the window base; otherwise it copies pcx_info.width bytes at pos. After the loop it returns 0. No bound is checked between pcx_info.bpsl or width and MAXSCANLINE in this function.
note: Slice 255-269 was only the tail of the function; the packet name pcx_banked_blit does not exist, the function is pcx_draw at splash_pcx.c:199-269 (read in full). Not dropped because the real function exists and only the name was wrong. Old prose claimed the function always returns 0 with no error path; the code has returns of 1 at 209, 239, 244.

name: fdt_foreach_mem_region
prose: Precondition: cb is a callback taking (struct mem_region *, void *arg) and OF/FDT accessors are usable. It returns ENXIO if the /memory node cannot be found; returns the error from fdt_addrsize_cells for the parent node if nonzero; returns ERANGE if the parent address cell count is more than 2, or if the length of the reg property is not positive or exceeds the local buffer; returns ENXIO if OF_getprop of reg returns <= 0. Otherwise it calls fdt_data_to_res on each complete (addr_cells + size_cells) tuple, returning its error immediately if nonzero (without calling cb for that tuple), and calls cb(&mr, arg) for each successfully converted tuple, ignoring cb's return value; trailing cells not forming a complete tuple are ignored; it returns 0 after the loop.
note: Slice was a window onto the function; real name fdt_foreach_mem_region at fdt_common.c:496-542 (read in full). Old prose said ERANGE when 'reg is absent' which matches reg_len <= 0 at 519-520. Not read: fdt_addrsize_cells and fdt_data_to_res internals.

name: vesa_set_mode
prose: Precondition: adp is a video adapter and mode is a requested mode number. If adp is not vesa_adp it returns the previous driver's set_mode result unchanged. Otherwise it maps the mode number with vesa_map_gen_mode_num. If the current mode is a VESA mode, the new mode is not a VESA mode and the previous driver's get_info accepts it, it resets the DAC to 6 bits if V_ADP_DAC8 was set, calls int10_set_mode(adp->va_initial_bios_mode) and, if the current mode info has V_INFO_LINEAR, unmaps the old linear buffer; this happens before the following steps and is not undone if they fail. If the new mode is not a VESA mode and the previous driver's set_mode returns 0 it returns 0. Otherwise it calls vesa_get_info and returns 1 if that fails. It then resets a 8-bit DAC if V_ADP_DAC8 is set, drops V_INFO_LINEAR for non-graphics modes, sets bit 0x4000 for a linear mode and calls vesa_bios_set_mode(mode | 0x8000), returning 1 if that fails (before the adapter state fields below are updated). On success it may switch the DAC to 8 bits (sets V_ADP_DAC8), unmaps the old linear buffer if the adapter's previous info had V_INFO_LINEAR, then updates va_mode (9 bits), the color flag, va_crtc_addr, va_line_width, the buffer, window, window size and granularity (mapping the linear frame buffer with pmap_mapdev_attr for a linear mode, otherwise using the BIOS window), va_buffer_size, window origin, display start and va_info, moves the hardware cursor off-screen with set_hw_cursor(-1, -1), and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the earlier path that leaves a VESA mode for a non-VESA mode calls int10_set_mode (vesa.c:1297-1308), and the DAC reset also occurs before vesa_bios_set_mode (1332-1335), so the failure paths can already have changed hardware. Original reviewer right that adp != vesa_adp forwards the previous driver's value (1280-1281). The line 1316 path returns 0 also when the non-VESA prev set_mode succeeds. Function at 1275-1412 (slice 1280-1539). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: vesa_save_state
prose: Precondition: adp is a video adapter, p a caller buffer of size bytes (size 0 queries the needed size). It returns the previous driver's save_state(adp, p, size) result if adp is not vesa_adp, or if size is 0 and vesa_state_buf_size is 0. Otherwise it computes bsize = offsetof(adp_state_t, regs) + vesa_state_buf_size; if size is 0 it returns bsize; if vesa_state_buf_size > 0 and size < bsize it returns EINVAL. Otherwise it frees any existing vesa_vmem_buf; then, only if the current mode is a VESA mode and adp->va_buffer is non-NULL, it tries to allocate adp->va_buffer_size bytes (M_NOWAIT) into vesa_vmem_buf and copies the frame buffer into it when the allocation succeeds (on failure vesa_vmem_buf stays NULL and the save continues). Finally if vesa_state_buf_size is 0 it returns the previous driver's save_state result, else it stores V_STATE_SIG in p and returns the result of vesa_bios_save_restore(STATE_SAVE, p->regs).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the frame buffer copy happens only for a VESA mode with va_buffer != NULL and a successful malloc (vesa.c:1493-1501). Original reviewer's complaint (size == 0 or too-small with vesa_state_buf_size == 0 delegates to the previous driver) is consistent with 1480-1486 and was already stated; EINVAL applies only when vesa_state_buf_size > 0. Function at 1474-1506 (slice 1280-1539). Read in full.

name: sbp_recv1
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the sbp softc lock (SBP_LOCK_ASSERT) and xfer->sc is the sbp_softc. It jumps to done0 without processing any status if xfer->resp is nonzero, the payload is NULL, the received packet is not a FWTCODE_WREQB write request, the target number from the destination address is >= SBP_NUM_TARGETS, or the LUN is out of range or has no sbp_dev. Otherwise it selects the OCB by status source: for src 0 or 1 it takes the target's current management OCB if it matches the status (stopping the management timeout and clearing mgm_ocb_cur), else dequeues one with sbp_dequeue_ocb (which may find none); src 2 (unsolicited) and unknown values leave ocb NULL. It computes status_valid0 (src < 2, response complete, not dead) and status_valid, logs unexpected statuses, and if the dead bit is set freezes the device queue (when it has a path, incrementing sdev->freeze) and sets reset_agent. If ocb is NULL it goes to done. Otherwise, for a standard-format ORB: a management OCB (OCB_ACT_MGM) clears reset_agent and then acts on the ORB function: login parses the login response and on valid status calls sbp_busy_timeout, else sets the device status to SBP_DEV_RESET; reconnect on valid status calls sbp_scan_dev if the device is attached, else sbp_agent_reset, and on failure calls sbp_login; logout sets the status to SBP_DEV_RESET; ORB_FUN_RST only calls sbp_busy_timeout; LUR, ATA and ATS call sbp_agent_reset; other values are logged; then it calls sbp_mgm_orb(sdev, ORB_FUN_RUNQUEUE, NULL). A command OCB (OCB_ACT_CMD) clears sdev->timeout and, if it has a ccb, sets the CAM status from the SCSI status (sbp_scsi_status when the status length is > 1, else CAM_REQ_CMP or CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR from the response), fixes INQUIRY data for INQUIRY commands and calls xpt_done. NOP and VED format ORBs do nothing. If use_doorbell is off the OCB is then freed with sbp_free_ocb. At done, if reset_agent is still set it calls sbp_agent_reset. At done0 (reached from all paths) it sets xfer->recv.pay_len to SBP_RECV_LEN and then, if NEED_RESPONSE is defined, builds a write response and sends it with fw_asyreq, otherwise appends the xfer to sbp->fwb.xferlist. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: ORB_FUN_RST only calls sbp_busy_timeout (sbp.c:1806-1808); old prose said the fetch agent is reset for reset functions. Original reviewer is right that the OCB is not always dequeued (src 2, unknown, or no match, 1657-1687). The early done0 paths also use rfp and sdev only under NEED_RESPONSE; not described further. Real function at 1598-1881 (slice 1547-1826). Read in full except the debug printf blocks, which were skipped.

name: sbp_probe_target
prose: Precondition: target is a valid sbp_target with a valid fwdev. It records whether the firewire device is alive (SBP_FWDEV_ALIVE), calls sbp_alloc_lun(target) to (re)build the LUN array, and then walks target->num_lun slots, skipping NULL slots. For a LUN whose status is not SBP_DEV_DEAD while the device is alive: if it has a path it freezes the device queue (incrementing sdev->freeze); it calls sbp_probe_lun and sbp_show_sdev_info; it takes the sbp lock only around sbp_abort_all_ocbs(sdev, CAM_SCSI_BUS_RESET); then if its status is SBP_DEV_RESET it calls sbp_login only when auto_login is set (otherwise it does nothing more), and for every other status (TOATTACH, PROBE, ATTACHED, RETRY and any other value) it sends an ORB_FUN_RCN management ORB with sbp_mgm_orb. For a LUN when the device is not alive or the LUN's status is SBP_DEV_DEAD: SBP_DEV_ATTACHED freezes the queue if it has a path (incrementing freeze), sets the status to SBP_DEV_RETRY, calls sbp_cam_detach_sdev and sbp_free_sdev and sets the slot to NULL; SBP_DEV_PROBE and SBP_DEV_TOATTACH are only set to SBP_DEV_RESET; SBP_DEV_RETRY, SBP_DEV_RESET and SBP_DEV_DEAD are left unchanged. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: a RESET LUN with auto_login off gets neither sbp_login nor ORB_FUN_RCN (sbp.c:718-723). Original reviewer right about the PROBE/TOATTACH dead case (749-752). Real function at 686-760 (slice 522-779). Read in full; callees not read.

name: scmi_virtio_poll_msg
prose: Precondition: dev is an attached scmi_virtio device, msg is a message submitted for polling, and tmo_ms is a timeout in milliseconds. It sets a loop budget N = tmo_ms / SCMI_VIRTIO_POLLING_INTERVAL_MS. The loop condition decrements the budget first and then, only if the budget was nonzero, checks msg->poll_done; each iteration calls virtio_scmi_message_poll; if no message is available it delays for the polling interval and continues; otherwise it maps the returned buffer to its message, sets that message's poll_done to 1 if its polling flag is set, leaves the loop if the returned message is msg, and for any other message that is not a polling one passes it to scmi_rx_irq_callback. The function returns 0 if the budget left after the loop is greater than zero and ETIMEDOUT otherwise. Consequently: when msg is returned by the poll on the k-th iteration it returns 0 only if k < N (returns ETIMEDOUT if it arrives on the last allowed iteration); when the loop ends because msg->poll_done was seen nonzero at the loop test it returns 0 only if at least two iterations of budget were left at that point; if N is 0 (tmo_ms below the interval) no poll is made, poll_done is not examined and it returns ETIMEDOUT.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that 'at least two iterations' is not the rule for the case where msg is returned by the poll (that case needs only one left, scmi_virtio.c:232-233 with 247); the two-iteration margin applies only to the poll_done test (216, post-decrement). Original reviewer also right that a message received on the last iteration gives ETIMEDOUT. Function at 205-248 (slice 1-255). Read in full; value of the polling interval constant not read.

name: inphy_service
prose: Precondition: sc is an attached inphy softc, mii its mii_data. For MII_MEDIACHG it calls mii_phy_setmedia(sc) only if the interface has IFF_UP set; when IFF_UP is clear it skips the media set but still continues to the status update below. For MII_TICK it returns 0 immediately if mii_phy_tick(sc) returns EJUSTRETURN, with no status update; otherwise it continues. For MII_POLLSTAT and for any other cmd value it continues without other action. On the continuing paths it calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd). It returns 0 in all cases.
note: Both reviewers right: the MII_TICK EJUSTRETURN case returns before PHY_STATUS (inphy.c:130-131), and MII_MEDIACHG with the interface down still reaches PHY_STATUS and mii_phy_update (123-124, 136-139), contrary to the old 'does nothing'. Function at 111-141 (slice 1-196). Read in full.

name: gpio_check_flags
prose: Precondition: caps and flags are arbitrary uint32_t values; no memory, lock or state is touched. It first masks flags with caps, then returns EINVAL if the masked value has both GPIO_PIN_INPUT and GPIO_PIN_OUTPUT, or both GPIO_PIN_PULLUP and GPIO_PIN_PULLDOWN, or GPIO_PIN_OUTPUT together with any bit of GPIO_INTR_MASK, or more than one bit of GPIO_INTR_MASK, or GPIO_INTR_ATTACHED; otherwise it returns 0.
note: Reviewer reasons were only mechanical (contract/syntax), no semantic claim to check. Prose checked against gpiobus.c:127-151, including the tests at 135-148. Contract left empty because the checks depend on macro flag values not expanded here.

name: hmt_intr
prose: Precondition: context is the hmt_softc and buf points to len readable bytes of a HID input report (len must be at least 1 when sc->report_id is nonzero). When built with IICHID_SAMPLING and sc->iichid_sampling is set, a zero-length report clears sc->prev_touch and sc->timestamp, calls evdev_sync and returns. Otherwise, if sc->report_id is nonzero it reads the first byte as the report id and returns without action when it differs from sc->report_id, else strips that byte. It reads the contact count (1 if the device has none) and, if the count is nonzero, stores it in sc->nconts_todo. It then processes MIN(sc->nconts_todo, sc->nconts_per_report) contacts: for each it extracts the usage values, maps the contact id to an evdev MT slot and skips the contact (with a debug message) if no slot is available (slot == -1); otherwise, if the tip switch is nonzero and the confidence usage (when present) is not zero, it sets sc->touch, computes distance, orientation, major and minor from width and height and pushes the slot data; else it pushes the slot with NULL data. It subtracts the processed count from sc->nconts_todo. When sc->do_timestamps is set and sc->nconts_todo has reached 0 it updates sc->timestamp from the scan time (delta computed only when sc->prev_touch was set), pushes MSC_TIMESTAMP, sets sc->prev_touch from sc->touch, clears sc->touch and zeroes sc->timestamp if there is no touch. When sc->nconts_todo is 0 it also pushes BTN_LEFT (from the internal and left buttons) and the other configured buttons and calls evdev_sync. The function returns nothing; no locks or memory are acquired or released here.
note: Packet name hmt_process_report does not exist; the real function is hmt_intr at hmt.c:495-674 (read in full), so it is fixed, not dropped. Original prose omitted the push with NULL data for non-touching contacts (632-635); the MSC_TIMESTAMP step only runs when do_timestamps is set (639). Reviewer reasons were only mechanical (name not in slice).

name: hpt_default_ioctl
prose: Precondition: lpInBuffer and lpOutBuffer point to buffers of the sizes given in nInBufferSize and nOutBufferSize (these sizes are checked per code, the buffer contents are trusted), and lpBytesReturned is NULL or writable. It switches on dwIoControlCode and returns -1 for an unknown code. Per code, returning -1 on a wrong size or a failing helper: GET_VERSION needs input size 0 and output size sizeof(DWORD) and stores HPT_INTERFACE_VERSION; GET_CONTROLLER_COUNT needs output size sizeof(DWORD); GET_CONTROLLER_INFO, GET_CHANNEL_INFO, GET_DEVICE_INFO and GET_DEVICE_INFO_V2 need exact input and output sizes (the device-info ones also reject INVALID_DEVICEID and zero the output first) and fail when the helper returns nonzero; GET_LOGICAL_DEVICES needs an input of one DWORD and an output of at least (1 + max) DWORDs and stores the helper's count. Under SUPPORT_ARRAY only: CREATE_ARRAY and CREATE_ARRAY_V2 need exact input size and output size sizeof(DEVICEID) and fail if the created id is INVALID_DEVICEID; SET_ARRAY_INFO, SET_DEVICE_INFO and ADD/REMOVE_SPARE_DISK need exact input size and output size 0; SET_DEVICE_INFO_V2 needs input at least the struct size and output 0; ADD_DISK_TO_ARRAY reads the two ids from the input before checking sizes, then needs exact input size and output size 0; SET_BOOT_MARK needs input size sizeof(DEVICEID) and walks every adapter's top-level devices, returning -1 if a device's vbus differs from the current vbus, clearing or setting the boot mark and calling SyncArrayInfo on the matching top device. GET_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES needs output size at least sizeof(DRIVER_CAPABILITIES). GET_CONTROLLER_VENID finds the adapter with the given index (-1 if none or if output size is under 4), writes (pciConfigDeviceId << 16) | 0x11AB and returns 0 directly without setting *lpBytesReturned. EPROM_IO finds the adapter by index (-1 if none), checks the input size (16 bytes plus length for a write) and output size (length for a read), returns -1 if too small, otherwise performs sx508x_flash_access for read or write and returns 0 directly without setting *lpBytesReturned. For all other codes that succeed, if lpBytesReturned is non-NULL it is set to nOutBufferSize and the function returns 0.
note: Packet name ioctl_dispatcher does not exist; the real function is hpt_default_ioctl at gui_lib.c:1123-1445, read in full. Old prose omitted the early checks for GET_VERSION/CONTROLLER_COUNT/INFO cases and the SUPPORT_ARRAY conditional (1231, 1375); ADD_DISK_TO_ARRAY reading before size check is at 1365-1368. Helper functions not read. The input pointers are dereferenced without checking input sizes for GET_CONTROLLER_VENID and EPROM_IO (1389, 1409-1412), unchanged.

name: hpt_create_array_v2
prose: Precondition: pParam is non-NULL; when pParam->nDisk is 0 the code still reads Members[0] (line 584), which is not checked, so nDisk should be at least 1. It first returns INVALID_DEVICEID, before allocating anything, if nDisk > MAX_MEMBERS, if any member fails check_VDevice_valid, is itself an array or is not online, if the members are not all on one vbus, or if the first member's vbus pointer is NULL. It then allocates an array table with mArGetArrayTable and returns INVALID_DEVICEID if that gives NULL. By ArrayType it sets the device type: JBOD; RAID0 and RAID5 (both need BlockSizeShift within [MinBlockSizeShift, MaxBlockSizeShift], else go to error; RAID5 also sets rf_need_rebuild unless CAF_CREATE_R5_NO_BUILD is given); RAID1 (with at most 2 disks a plain mirror, otherwise a RAID0 of nDisk/2 RAID1 child arrays built from pairs of members); any other type goes to error. It fills the array fields, attaches the members (setting their parent and serial number and unregistering them, except the first member in a CAF_CREATE_AND_DUPLICATE RAID1), sets each member's pfnDeviceFailed, and for CAF_CREATE_AND_DUPLICATE RAID1 transfers the boot flags and, if the first member was found in the vbus slot table, installs the array in that slot (so RegisterVDevice is skipped), otherwise clears boot flags on all disks and zeroes sector 0 of each with fDeReadWrite. It then marks the array online and computes VDeviceCapacity per type (RAID0, RAID1, JBOD, RAID5), sets the command and failure callbacks, calls SyncArrayInfo, calls RegisterVDevice unless the array was installed in the vbus slot, and returns VDEV_TO_ID(pArray). At the error label (reached from the block-size, unknown type and capacity switch failures after the table was allocated) it frees each member entry that is not a single disk with mArFreeArrayTable, frees the array table and returns INVALID_DEVICEID; the earlier validation and allocation failures return INVALID_DEVICEID without calling mArFreeArrayTable.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the early failures (nDisk > MAX_MEMBERS, member checks, NULL pVBus, NULL array table) return at hpt gui_lib.c:569-588 without mArFreeArrayTable. Original reviewer is right that Members[0] is dereferenced at 584 before any nDisk check. Function at 561-809 (slice 506-765). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: pmc_save_user_callchain
prose: Precondition: tf is a user-mode trap frame (KASSERTed with TRAPF_USERMODE), cc points to storage for the samples. It always writes the trap frame PC to cc[0], even when maxsamples is 0 or 1, and returns 1 if maxsamples <= 1. Otherwise it takes fp from the trap frame and returns 1 if either the PC or the frame pointer is not in user space (PMC_IN_USERSPACE). Then, starting with count 1, while count < maxsamples it reads the saved return address at fp + sizeof(uintptr_t) with copyin and stops if the copy fails or the value is not in user space; otherwise it appends it to cc; it then reads the previous frame pointer from fp with copyin and stops if the copy fails, if the new fp is below the old fp (equal is allowed) or if it is not in user space; otherwise count is incremented and the loop continues. The function returns count; because the count is incremented only at the end of a complete iteration, when the loop stops after a return address has been appended (failed fp copy or bad new fp) the returned count is one less than the number of entries written to cc.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: count++ is skipped on the break paths at hwpmc_arm64_md.c:122-125 after cc was written at 117, so the return can be less than the entries written. Round 1 reviewer is right that equal fp values are allowed (124 uses fp < oldfp); round 2 right that maxsamples 0 still writes cc[0] and returns 1 (97-101). Function at 87-129. Read in full.

name: hvsock_canread_check
prose: Precondition: pcb may be NULL; if non-NULL, pcb->so is valid and pcb->chan may be NULL. Returns 0 if pcb is NULL; returns 0 after setting pcb->so->so_error to EIO if pcb->chan is NULL; returns the pending pcb->recv_data_len if it is greater than 0. Otherwise it sets advance to the length of the previous packet when pcb->rb_init is set, else 0, and reads the readable byte count of the channel ring. If rb_init is set and exactly advance + 8 bytes are readable it advances the ring index by advance with vmbus_chan_recv_idxadv: on error it returns 0 (rb_init unchanged); on success it clears rb_init, zeroes recv_data_len and recv_data_off, re-reads the readable count, returns 0 if nothing is readable, else resets advance to 0. It returns 0 if fewer than advance + sizeof(struct hvs_pkt_header) + 8 bytes are readable, or if vmbus_chan_recv_peek of the header fails. It validates the peeked header (header length at least the channel packet header size, not above total length, total length at least data length plus the header size); if invalid it sets so_error to EIO and returns 0. Otherwise it sets rb_init to true, sets so_error to ESHUTDOWN when the data length is 0 (FIN), stores the data length in recv_data_len, sets recv_data_off to 0 and returns the data length (0 for a FIN).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: vmbus_chan_recv_idxadv failure returns 0 (hv_sock.c:1286-1291) and the old prose lacked that case. Real function is hvsock_canread_check at 1243-1362 (slice 1274-1532 cut the head). Read in full.

name: hv_hid_receive
prose: Precondition: sc is an initialised hv_hid_sc and pkt is a received inband channel packet whose payload begins with an hv_hid_msg. It returns nothing. It returns at once if msg->type is not HV_HID_MSG_DATA, and after printing a message if the payload length is not greater than sizeof(hv_hid_pmsg). Otherwise by sub-message type: SH_PROTO_RESP calls vmbus_xact_ctx_wakeup with the packet payload if sc->hs_xact_ctx is non-NULL, else does nothing. SH_DEVINFO builds an ack and calls vmbus_xact_get(sc->hs_xact_ctx, ...); if that returns NULL it stops (without parsing the device info); otherwise it sends the ack on sc->hs_chan (result ignored) and releases the transaction, then stops if sc->rdesc is already non-NULL, if hdesc->bLength is 0, or if the report descriptor length is 0 (in which last case sc->hdi has already been zeroed and has rdescsize 0); otherwise it fills sc->hdi (name, bus, vendor, product, version), allocates a zeroed buffer of rdescsize bytes with M_WAITOK, copies the report descriptor into it, and under sc->mtx stores it in sc->rdesc and calls wakeup(sc). SH_INPUT_REPORT takes sc->mtx and, if sc->intr is non-NULL and sc->intr_on is set, calls sc->intr with the report buffer and size, then releases sc->mtx. Any other sub-message type does nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the vmbus_xact_get failure breaks before any parsing (hv_hid.c:278-280). Round 2 reviewer right: rdescsize 0 leaves sc->hdi zeroed (297-300), and SH_PROTO_RESP wakes a waiter (253-262). Original reviewer right that rdesc is not always set (288-300). Function at 233-328 (slice 256-511).

name: iavf_asq_send_command
prose: Precondition: hw is a valid iavf_hw, desc points to a descriptor in ordinary memory, buff is NULL or points to buff_size bytes, cmd_details is NULL or valid. It takes hw->aq.asq_spinlock and releases it on every return path, sets asq_last_status to IAVF_AQ_RC_OK, and sends nothing and returns an error in these cases: IAVF_ERR_QUEUE_EMPTY if asq.count is 0, or if the head register value is >= num_asq_entries; then (after copying or clearing the command details and applying details->flags_dis and flags_ena to desc->flags and setting the cookie when given) IAVF_ERR_INVALID_SIZE if buff_size > asq_buf_size, IAVF_ERR_PARAM if postpone is set without async, and IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_FULL if iavf_clean_asq finds no free descriptor. Otherwise it copies desc into the ring descriptor at next_to_use, copies the buffer (when given) into the matching DMA buffer and sets datalen and the buffer address, advances next_to_use with wrap, writes the tail register unless postpone is set, and unless async or postpone is set polls iavf_asq_done every 50 us until done or asq_cmd_timeout. If the command is done it copies the descriptor (and the buffer, when given) back to the caller, takes the descriptor's return value (masked to 8 bits if nonzero), sets asq_last_status to it and returns IAVF_SUCCESS for IAVF_AQ_RC_OK, IAVF_ERR_NOT_READY for IAVF_AQ_RC_EBUSY and IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_ERROR otherwise. If details->wb_desc is set the ring descriptor is copied to it after queueing. If not done and neither async nor postpone is set, it returns IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_CRITICAL_ERROR when the ATQCRIT bit is set in the length register and IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_TIMEOUT otherwise; if not done with async or postpone it returns IAVF_SUCCESS.
note: Rounds 15 and 17 reviewers are wrong: the head >= num_asq_entries check returns IAVF_ERR_QUEUE_EMPTY at iavf_adminq.c:695-701 and the IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_FULL path exists at 754-760; the earlier prose had them right. Added that desc->flags is modified before the size and postpone checks (727-728). Real function at 670-866 (slice 762-989 cut head). Read in full; iavf_clean_asq and iavf_asq_done not read.

name: iavf_process_adminq
prose: Precondition: sc and its hw are valid, sc->aq_buffer is at least IAVF_AQ_BUF_SZ bytes, and pending is non-NULL (it is dereferenced in the loop test). If IAVF_STATE_RESET_PENDING is set it sets status IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_ERROR; otherwise if iavf_check_aq_errors reports an error it sets IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_CRITICAL_ERROR; in both cases it skips to the interrupt re-enable without taking the VC lock and without writing *pending. Otherwise it clears sc->aq_buffer, takes the VC lock and loops: it calls iavf_clean_arq_element(hw, &event, pending) and breaks with that status if nonzero, otherwise calls iavf_vc_completion with the message opcode, return value, buffer and length and clears the buffer; the loop continues while *pending is nonzero and loop++ < IAVF_ADM_LIMIT, so it can handle up to IAVF_ADM_LIMIT + 1 elements per call. It releases the VC lock, and on every path reaches the label that sets the IAVF_VFINT_ICR0_ENA1_ADMINQ_MASK bit in IAVF_VFINT_ICR0_ENA1. It returns the status (IAVF_SUCCESS if the loop ended with the last clean call succeeding, or the failing status).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the do/while test loop++ < IAVF_ADM_LIMIT lets IAVF_ADM_LIMIT + 1 passes run (if_iavf_iflib.c:1220-1231). Original reviewer right that *pending is not written on the early paths (1202-1211). Function at 1192-1241 (slice 1036-1300). Read in full; iavf_clean_arq_element and iavf_vc_completion not read.

name: ice_bitmap_from_array32
prose: Precondition: dst points to a bitmap of at least size bits, src points to an array of u32 words with ceil(size / 32) readable entries. It first calls ice_zero_bitmap(dst, size) (what that call clears was not read), then for each of the size / 32 full words in src it sets, with ice_set_bit, every dst bit at index word * 32 + j for which bit j of the word is set. If size % 32 is nonzero it then reads the next word src[size / 32] and sets the dst bits for its lowest size % 32 bits that are set. The function returns nothing and takes no locks; src is not modified.
note: The packet item ice_bitmap_copy does not exist anywhere under sys/dev/ice (grep finds no match); slice 507-539 is the tail of ice_bitmap_from_array32 at ice_bitops.h:498-532 (read in full), so it is fixed under that real name rather than dropped. The old prose described a copy that this code does not do. ice_zero_bitmap and ice_set_bit were not read.

name: ice_clean_rq_elem
prose: Precondition: hw, cq and e are valid, the caller does not hold cq->rq_lock, e->msg_buf (if non-NULL) has room for e->buf_len bytes, and pending is NULL or points to a u16. It zeroes e->desc first, then takes cq->rq_lock. If cq->rq.count is 0 it returns ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY without writing *pending. It reads the hardware head (masked by head_mask); if it equals next_to_clean it returns ICE_ERR_AQ_NO_WORK with the ring state unchanged and *pending still updated when pending is non-NULL. Otherwise it takes the descriptor at next_to_clean; if its ICE_AQ_FLAG_ERR flag is set it records ICE_ERR_AQ_ERROR and logs, but continues; it copies the descriptor into e->desc, sets e->msg_len to MIN(datalen, e->buf_len), copies that many bytes from the ring buffer to e->msg_buf when msg_buf is non-NULL and msg_len is nonzero, then zeroes the ring descriptor and rewrites its flags (ICE_AQ_FLAG_BUF, plus ICE_AQ_FLAG_LB for large buffers), datalen and buffer address, writes next_to_clean to the tail register, advances next_to_clean with wrap at num_rq_entries and sets cq->rq.next_to_use to the head value read. In every case except ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY it sets *pending (when non-NULL) to the number of descriptors still pending computed from a fresh head read. It releases cq->rq_lock on every return and returns 0, ICE_ERR_AQ_ERROR (after full processing of the descriptor), ICE_ERR_AQ_NO_WORK or ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY.
note: Both reviewers (rounds 15 and 17) are wrong: the error flag only sets ret_code and the copy, rewrite, tail write and next_to_clean update still run (ice_controlq.c:1283-1318); e->desc is zeroed at 1257 and then overwritten with the ring descriptor at 1288 (both statements are true), and the ring descriptor is also zeroed at 1302. Real function at 1242-1331 (slice 1295-1331 was only the tail). Read in full.

name: ice_sched_add_rl_profile
prose: Precondition: hw is an ice_hw whose scheduler lock is held by the caller (not checked here), and rl_type, bw and layer_num select the profile. It returns NULL, with nothing allocated, if hw is NULL, if layer_num >= hw->num_tx_sched_layers, or if rl_type is not ICE_MIN_BW, ICE_MAX_BW or ICE_SHARED_BW (mapped to profile types CIR, EIR and SRL). It then scans hw->rl_prof_list[layer_num] and returns the first existing entry whose profile type matches and whose bw equals bw, without changing that entry (prof_id_ref is not touched here). Otherwise it allocates a new element (NULL on failure), converts bw into a profile with ice_sched_bw_to_rl_profile, sets bw, profile.level = layer_num + 1, profile.flags = the profile type and profile.max_burst_size from hw->max_burst_size, and calls ice_aq_add_rl_profile for exactly one profile. If the conversion fails, the AQ call fails, or profiles_added is not 1, it frees the new element and returns NULL. On success it sets prof_id_ref to 0, adds the element at the head of hw->rl_prof_list[layer_num] and returns it. The returned pointer is owned by the list.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: the existing-profile path at ice_sched.c:4105-4110 returns the entry without any prof_id_ref update; only the new-profile path sets prof_id_ref to 0 (4137). Real function at 4079-4144 (slice 4112-4375 cut the head). Read in full; ice_sched_bw_to_rl_profile and ice_aq_add_rl_profile not read.

name: ice_add_mac_with_sw_marker
prose: Precondition: hw is valid with hw->switch_info and hw->port_info set; f_info describes the filter. It returns ICE_ERR_PARAM if f_info->fltr_act is not ICE_FWD_TO_VSI, the lookup type is not ICE_SW_LKUP_MAC, sw_marker is ICE_INVAL_SW_MARKER_ID or the vsi_handle is not valid; otherwise it sets f_info->fwd_id.hw_vsi_id and calls ice_add_mac_rule: ICE_ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS marks the entry as pre-existing, any other nonzero result is returned at once. It then takes the MAC recipe's filt_rule_lock and looks up the entry. It reaches the error exit if the entry is not found, if its counter_index is valid (ret = ICE_ERR_PARAM), if its sw_marker_id already equals sw_marker (ret = ICE_ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS), if ice_alloc_res_lg_act fails (ret is its error), if the allocated lg_act_id equals ICE_INVAL_LG_ACT_INDEX (ret keeps its previous value), or if ice_add_marker_act fails. On success of ice_add_marker_act it releases the lock and returns 0. At the error exit it releases the lock and, if the filter was added by this call (not pre-existing), returns the result of ice_remove_mac instead of the earlier error; if the filter pre-existed it returns the value ret has at that point, which is ICE_ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS when the entry is not found, and 0 when the lg_act_id was invalid. So the function can return 0 without installing the marker (pre-existing filter and invalid lg_act_id), and a failed marker installation on a newly added filter returns the removal status, which may be 0.
note: Both reviewers right: invalid lg_act_id (ice_switch.c:4037-4038) and cleanup both can give 0 without the marker. Also the rule lock is released on every path after it is taken (4043, 4048). Function at 3966-4054 (slice 3878-4128). Read in full; callees not read.

name: ice_poll_for_media_avail
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid ice_softc with hw->port_info set. On an E830 device with ICE_STATE_PHY_FW_INIT_PENDING set: if GL_MNG_FWSM_FW_LOADING_M is set in GL_MNG_FWSM it clears ICE_STATE_PHY_FW_INIT_PENDING and continues, otherwise it returns immediately. Then if ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA is not set it does nothing more (the E830 step may already have cleared the pending state). If ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA is set it sets pi->phy.get_link_info to true and calls ice_get_link_status, which refreshes sc->link_up and the link info whether or not media is available. If the link info then has ICE_AQ_MEDIA_AVAILABLE set: when ICE_STATE_LINK_ACTIVE_ON_DOWN is set or the interface has IFF_UP, it calls ice_apply_saved_phy_cfg(sc, ICE_APPLY_LS_FEC_FC) (result ignored) and ice_add_media_types, printing an error message if the latter fails; in either case it then clears ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA. If media is not available, ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA stays set. The function returns nothing and takes no locks itself.
note: Both reviewers right: the E830 branch can clear PHY_FW_INIT_PENDING (if_ice_iflib.c:2206-2212) and get_link_info/link_up change even when media is unavailable (2215-2216). Reapply/add-media is gated by LINK_ACTIVE_ON_DOWN or IFF_UP (2222-2223), while clearing NO_MEDIA is not (2235). Function at 2196-2238 (slice 2042-2299). Read in full; callees not read, and the prose no longer claims the caller's lock state.

name: icintr
prose: Precondition: dev is an ic(4) device with softc sc; the caller does not hold sc->ic_lock (the function takes it with mtx_lock on entry and releases it before returning). event is dispatched: INTR_GENERAL and INTR_START reset the input pointer and transfer count and set IC_IFBUF_BUSY; INTR_STOP clears IC_IFBUF_BUSY and wakes a buffer waiter if only IC_BUFFER_WAITER is set among the busy/waiter flags; then if error count ic_iferrs is nonzero or the transferred length is at most ICHDRLEN (but nonzero) it logs the errors, resets ic_iferrs and increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS; a zero-length transfer is ignored; otherwise it increments IFCOUNTER_IPACKETS and IBYTES, taps BPF, builds an mbuf with m_devget and, only if that succeeds, drops the lock around netisr_dispatch(NETISR_IP) inside the network epoch and re-takes it (if m_devget fails, the counters have still been incremented and the frame is dropped silently). INTR_RECEIVE stores one byte from *ptr and advances unless the transfer count is already at least MTU + ICHDRLEN, in which case it only increments ic_iferrs. INTR_NOACK does nothing. INTR_TRANSMIT writes 0xff to *ptr. INTR_ERROR increments ic_iferrs. Any other event panics. For all handled events it releases the lock and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right on both points: the lock is acquired inside (ic.c:274) not held on entry, and IPACKETS/IBYTES are incremented before m_devget (300-303) so an m_devget failure still counts. Original reviewer right that an m_devget failure drops the packet without netisr dispatch. Function at 267-347 (slice 264-433). Read in full.

name: ds1307_sqw_freq_sysctl
prose: Precondition: arg1 points to an initialised ds1307 softc; oidp and req are the sysctl handler arguments (arg2 is unused). It reads the control register with ds1307_ctrl_read and returns the error if that fails. It takes the RS field of sc_ctrl as an index into the table {1, 4096, 8192, 32768} (clamped to the last entry if out of range) and passes that frequency to sysctl_handle_int(oidp, &freq, 0, req); if that returns an error or the request has no new value (newptr is NULL) it returns that result without writing the device. If the new value differs from the current table frequency, it picks the largest table index whose frequency is <= the new value (index 0, 1 Hz, if the value is below 1), replaces the RS bits in sc_ctrl, and writes the control register with ds1307_ctrl_write, returning its error if nonzero (sc_ctrl has already been modified in that case). If the value is unchanged it returns 0 without a write.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: oidp is passed to sysctl_handle_int at ds1307.c:174, so it is not unused. Original reviewer right that a value below 1 selects index 0 (178-181). Function at 159-190 (slice 1-253). Read in full.

name: ds1775_sensor_sysctl
prose: Precondition: arg1 is the device_t of an attached ds1775 whose softc is valid; oidp and req are the sysctl handler arguments. It reads the temperature with ds1775_sensor_read(sc); if the value is negative it returns EIO without calling sysctl_handle_int. Otherwise it calls sysctl_handle_int(oidp, &temp, 0, req) and returns that call's result. It takes no locks itself.
note: Packet name ds1775_temp_sysctl_handler does not exist; the real function is ds1775_sensor_sysctl at ds1775.c:250-268 (read in full), so it is fixed under that name. Reviewer reasons were only mechanical. Whether ds1775_sensor_read can itself return a value that sysctl_handle_int treats specially was not read.

name: irdma_sc_suspend_resume_qps
prose: Precondition: vsi is a valid irdma_sc_vsi whose qos[i].qos_mutex and qplist are initialised for i < IRDMA_MAX_USER_PRIORITY. For each user priority it takes qos[i].qos_mutex, walks every qp on that priority's list, and releases the mutex before the next priority. For op == IRDMA_OP_RESUME, a qp that is not suspended is skipped; for a suspended one it calls qp->dev->ws_add(vsi, i): if ws_add returns 0 (success) it sets qp->qs_handle from irdma_get_qp_qs and issues the CQP resume, clearing qp->suspended only if the CQP call returns 0 (qs_handle stays updated even if the CQP call fails); if ws_add returns nonzero it still issues the CQP resume (clearing suspended only on CQP success, qs_handle unchanged) and then calls irdma_modify_qp_to_err(qp). For op == IRDMA_OP_SUSPEND, only a qp in IRDMA_QP_STATE_RTS or IRDMA_QP_STATE_RTR gets a CQP suspend, and only if that returns 0 does it increment vsi->qp_suspend_reqs and set qp->suspended. For any other op value nothing is changed, but the lists are still walked under the mutexes. The function returns nothing and holds no mutex on return.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that qs_handle is updated on the ws_add success path before the CQP result is known (irdma_ctrl.c:122-125), and irdma_modify_qp_to_err runs on the ws_add failure path regardless of the CQP result (126-130). Original reviewer right that suspension state changes only when the CQP call succeeds. Function at 106-144 (slice 1-257). Read in full; callees not read.

name: sati_inquiry_translate_command
prose: Precondition: sequence, scsi_io and ata_io are valid and the CDB of scsi_io can be read. If the EVPD bit in CDB byte 1 is clear and the page code (byte 2) is nonzero, it builds CHECK CONDITION sense data (ILLEGAL REQUEST, invalid field in CDB) and returns SATI_FAILURE_CHECK_RESPONSE_DATA. Otherwise it sets sequence->allocation_length from CDB bytes 3 and 4 (this happens before the EVPD branch, so also on the supported-pages and unsupported-page paths). If EVPD is set: the supported-pages page sets sequence->type to SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_SUPPORTED_PAGES, builds the response data with sati_inquiry_supported_pages_translate_data and returns SATI_COMPLETE without constructing an ATA command; the unit serial number, device ID and block device pages set the corresponding sequence type; the ATA information page, when sequence->state is SATI_SEQUENCE_STATE_INCOMPLETE, constructs an EXECUTE DEVICE DIAGNOSTIC command in ata_io and sets type SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_EXECUTE_DEVICE_DIAG, otherwise sets type SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_ATA_INFORMATION; any other page code builds the same ILLEGAL REQUEST sense data and returns SATI_FAILURE_CHECK_RESPONSE_DATA. If EVPD is clear the type is set to SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_STANDARD. For all those non-returning cases it then calls sati_ata_identify_device_construct(ata_io, sequence) (also after the EXECUTE DEVICE DIAGNOSTIC construction in the incomplete ATA-information case) and returns SATI_SUCCESS.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right on both points: allocation_length is set at sati_inquiry.c:683-684 before the EVPD switch, and in the incomplete ATA-information case both the diagnostic constructor (711) and the identify constructor (745) are called. Original reviewer right that the supported-pages path returns SATI_COMPLETE (693-696). Function at 656-748 (slice 523-773). Read in full; construct helpers not read.

name: scic_controller_set_mode
prose: Precondition: controller is a controller handle. If the controller state machine is in SCI_BASE_CONTROLLER_STATE_INITIALIZING or SCI_BASE_CONTROLLER_STATE_INITIALIZED, then for operating_mode SCI_MODE_SPEED it sets each of remote_node_entries, task_context_entries, the unsolicited frame buffer count, completion_event_entries and completion_queue_entries to the minimum of its current value and the speed-mode constants (SCI_MAX_REMOTE_DEVICES, SCU_IO_REQUEST_COUNT, SCU_UNSOLICITED_FRAME_COUNT, SCU_EVENT_COUNT, SCU_COMPLETION_QUEUE_COUNT), rebuilds the memory descriptor table and returns SCI_SUCCESS; for SCI_MODE_SIZE it does the same with the size-mode constants (SCI_MIN_REMOTE_DEVICES, SCI_MIN_IO_REQUESTS, SCU_MIN_UNSOLICITED_FRAMES, SCU_MIN_EVENTS, SCU_MIN_COMPLETION_QUEUE_ENTRIES) and returns SCI_SUCCESS; for any other mode it returns SCI_FAILURE_INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE without changing the controller. In any other controller state it returns SCI_FAILURE_INVALID_STATE without changing the controller.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the old text required the two states as a precondition while also documenting the other-state return; the precondition is dropped (scic_sds_controller.c:4508-4553). Original reviewer's 'size mode clamps to minimums' point matches 4532-4545 and is now stated by constant names. Function at 4493-4556 (slice 4340-4591). Read in full.
